title: Cc No. 734/12, Dscf vs Gopi Chand on 25 April, 2013
full_text: Cc No. 734/12, Dscf vs Gopi Chand on 25 April, 2013 1 IN THE COURT OF SHRI JAGMOHAN SINGH, MM (NI ACT) ­ 08 DWARKA COURTS NEW DELHI CC NO: 734/12 Unique Case ID No: R0066122011 Delhi Schedule Castes Financial & Development Corporation Ltd. (A Government of Delhi Corporation) 2, Battery Lane, Rajpur Road, Delhi­54 .............................. Complainant Versus Gopi Chand S/o Sh. Vajir Chand r/o H­108,, Harkesh Nagar, New Delhi­110020 ................................ Accused 1. Name of the complainant : Delhi Schedule Castes Financial & Development Corporation Ltd 2. Name of the accused : Gopi Chand 3. Offence Complained of or proved : Under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 4. Plea of the Accused : Pleaded not guilty 5. Date of filing : 23.08.2000 6. Date of Institution : 26.08.2000 7. Date of reserving judgment/order : 09.04.2013 8. Final Order/Judgment : Acquittal 9. Date of pronouncement : 20.04.2013 CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 2 JUDGMENT BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR THE DECISION OF THE CASE:­ 1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present complaint u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act filed by the complainant against the accused. 2. The case of the complainant is that the complainant is a Government Undertaking controlled and financed by Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi. The accused had taken and received a loan from the complainant. The accused issued three cheques bearing No. 312598 dated 01.02.2002, for Rs. 9568/­, cheque bearing no. 312599 dated 01.03.2002 for Rs. 9529/­ and cheque bearing no. 312600 dated 02.04.2002 for Rs. 9492/­ each drawn on Dena Bank, Okhla Indutrial Estate, New Delhi Branch. The aforesaid cheques when presented for payment were returned dishonoured vide a common return memo dated 27.06.2002 with the remarks "Funds Insufficient". Thereafter, the complainant sent a legal demand notice dated 11.07.2002 through registered post dated 31.07.2002 to the accused. However, as per the complainant, despite service of the said legal notice of demand, the accused failed to pay the aforesaid dishonoured cheque. Hence, the present complainant. 3. The cognizance of offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 was taken by the Ld. Predecessor Court and accused was summoned vide order dated 26.10.2002. The accused appeared in Court and was admitted to bail. Thereafter, separate notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C . explaining accusations CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 3 against the accused u/s 138 of the NI Act was framed against the accused on 14.5.2012, to which he did not plead guilty and claimed trial. 4. An application filed by the accused u/s 145(2) NI Act seeking cross examination of the complainant witneses was allowed. Accordingly, AR of the complainant was cross examined by the accused. On the statement of AR of the complainant, CE was closed vide order dated 31.08.2012. Thereafter, the statement of the accused u/s 313Cr.P.C was recorded on 15.09.2012. Accused filed an application u/s 315 Cr.P.C seeking permission of the Court to examined himself as DW. The same was allowed and accused examined himself as DW1. 5. Documents relied upon by the complainant are as follows:­(i)Ex.CW1/A : A copy of authorisation letter in favour of the first AR; (ii) Ex.CW1/B: Original cheque bearing no. 312598 dated 01.02.2002 for Rs.9568/­ (iii) Ex.CW1/C: cheque no. 312599 dated 01.03.2002 for Rs.9529/­ (iv) Ex.CW1/D:cheque bearing no. 312600 dated 02.04.2002 for Rs. 9492/­ (all drawn on Dena Bank Okhla Estate, New Delhi, Branch) (v) Ex. CW­1/E: Original Cheque returning memos (vi) Ex. CW­1/F: Copy of Legal Notice dated 11.07.2002; and (vii) Ex.CW1/G: A copy of register maintained in the post office as postal receipt (viii) Ex. CW­1/J : a copy of the authority letter issued by the complainant in favour of the new AR (ix) Ex.CW1/K (colly): Statement of account of accused 6. It is well settled position that to constitute an offence under S. 138 N.I. Act, the following ingredients are required to be fulfilled: (i) a person must have drawn a cheque on an account maintained by him in a bank for payment of a certain amount of money to another person from out of CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 4 that account; (ii) The cheque should have been issued for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability; (iii) that cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier; (iv) that cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of the account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with the bank; (v) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within 30 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; (vi) the drawer of such cheque fails to make payment of the said amount of money to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the said notice. 7. Being cumulative, it is only when all the aforementioned ingredients are satisfied that the person who had drawn the cheque can be deemed to have committed an offence under Section 138 of the Act. 8. During the examination of the accused u/s 313 Cr.P.C the accused admitted the fact that he had purchased a Tempo Traveller on Hire Purchase basis with the amount financed by the Complainant in February 1999. He also submitted that CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 5 the complainant gave rebate of 6 months from payment of installments and he made regular payment till May 2001. Thereafter, by order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court all Diesel driven vehicles were banned from plying in Delhi. He filed applications with the complainant that either the vehicle should be converted into CNG or the complainant should take back the same. The complainant did not respond so he along with other petitioners approached the Hon'ble High court of Delhi. He further submitted that in the year 2003 Hon'ble High Court passed a judgment in their favour as per which the complainant was directed to finance new vehicles to them (means the accused and other petitioners) within one month. He stated that he completed all the formalities but the complainant did not finance any new vehicle to him. He also submitted that the old Tempo Traveller wass lying idle at his house and was being wasted. 9. I have gone through the documents/evidence placed on record and have heard both the parties. The follwing questions arise for my consideration in the present case;­ (i) Whether prosecution of the present complaint was barred in terms of the order of Hon'ble High Court dated 26.02.2003 passed in Civil Writ Petition No. 4831/2002, Gopi Chand vs DSFDC Ltd. (ii) Whether the present complaint is maintainable. Discussion on question (i) and finding thereon 10. It is a matter of record that many petitioners, all of whom belonged to CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 6 SC/ST/Weaker sections of society, including accused Gopi Chand, filed Civil Writ Petitions before the Honble High Court in which they submitted that vide order dated 05.04.2002 passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in CWP No. 13029/85 filed by M C Mehta, all diesel buses/tempo travellers plying on diesel in National Capital Territory of Delhi were banned unless they were converted into CNG mode by specified dates. As the vehicles purchased by the petioners on hire purchase basis with the help of loan obtained from the Complainnt were diesel driven, the petitioners made the following prayers,­(i) The agreement between the petitioners and the respondent (Complainant herein) stood frustrated because of aforesaid order passsed by the Supreme Court as it had become impossible to perform and, therefore, it may be declared void under Section 56 of the Contracts Act; (ii) Balance outstanding amount of loan be waived off on the condition that the petitioners are ready to give back the possession of the hypothecated tempo travellers/diesel buses and same be auctioned by the respondent and whatever amount is received may be adjusted and further that petitioners and their guarntors be discharged from all liabliities; and (iii) Proceedings initiated against the petitioners u/s 138 of NI Act be dropped. 11. In the order dated 26.02.2003, Hon'ble High Court held that the respondent (Complainant) had already completed their part of the contract by making available the required funds to the petitioners and now the stage was only repayment of the above loans. Therefore, Section 56 of Contract Act would have no application. Taking note of the Scheme formulated by the Government CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 7 of NCT of Delhi for SC/ST and weaker sections pursuant to the order dated 5.04.2002 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in M C Mehta (supra), the Hon'ble High Court disposed of the CWPs with the following directions,­ (i)The petitioners shall be permitted to apply for finance/loans under the aforesaid scheme either for conversion of their existing vehicles into CNG fuel mode wherever possible or for purchase of new vehicle; (ii) the petitioners were to prefer applications within two weeks from the date of receipt of the order and the respondent (Complainant) was to consider the applications and take decision within two months thereafter depending upon merits of each case; and (iii) till such deicision was taken, the respondent (Complainant) were not to pursue the complaints filed by them u/s 138 NI Act against the petitioners. 12.It was submitted by the Ld. Defense Counsel that the accused submitted application to the complainant within time in terms of the order of the Hon'ble High Court but the Complainant did not take any action on the same. He further submitted that, therefore, the Complainant was not entitled to prosecute the present complaint case and the same was liable to be dismissed. 13.On the contrary, it was submited by Ld. Counsel for the Complainant that the accused did not file the application within the time stipulated under the order of Hon'ble High Court. He further submitted that it was held by the Hon'ble High Court that each case was to be decided on its merits and therefore, the Complainant was not bound to convert each and every vehicle into CNG mode. Lastly it was submitted that in any case, as held by the Hon'ble High Court, the CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 8 loan already granted could not be waived of and the accused could not escape liablility. 14. The above rival contentions may now be dealt with. It may be seen from the above order that the Hon'ble High Court did not grant any stay in the present case. The Hon'ble High Court only directed the respondent (Complainant) not to pursue the present complaint for a particular period of time to enable the accused to file application in terms of the said order and its consideration on merits by the Complainant. It was also held by the Hon'ble High Court that the loan already granted could not be waived of. Accused filed a copy of applications along with affidavits submitted to the complainant as Mark A to K to support the plea that he had appreached the complainant for conversion of his tempo traveller into CNG mode. On the face of it, its clear that applications Mark H filed in the year 2001, Mark I dated 29.03.2001 and two applications Mark G and J dated 10.04.2001 were filed much prior to the passing of above order dated 26.02.2003 by the Hon'ble High Court and are not relevant for the purpose of the present discussion. Similarly, application Mark A dated 05.05.2003, three applications dated 14.05.2003 each as Mark D, E and F and application Mark C dated 27.01.2004 were also apparently filed much beyond the stipulated period of two weeks from the above order. The accused has not deposed anything as to when he received the certified copy of the above order. Thus he did not bring on record complete facts/documents to enable this Court to form an opinion as to whether the accused had approached the Complainant within time in terms of the Hon'ble High Court order dated 26.02.2003. In CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 9 any case, if the accused filed the application timely and the Complainant did not respond, as claimed by him, it was for the accused to approach the Hon'ble High Court for relief but he did not do so. 15. To say the least, it is beyond the jurisdiction of this Court to give a finding as to which party committed default in compliance of the order of the Hon'ble High Court. That jurisdiction vests in the Hon'ble High Court alone. 16. In the above circumstances, I hold that the prosecution of the present complaint was not barred in terms of the order of Hon'ble High Court dated 26.02.2003 passed in Writ Petition No. 4831/2002. Discussion on question (ii) and finding thereon 17. There are three cheque in question which were returned unpaid vide a common return memo Exh CW­1/E dated 27.06.2002. The legal notice Exh CW1/F is dated 11.07.2002 and the same was sent to the accused on 31.07.2002 as per the copy of proof of dispatch CW1/G. 18.Ld. Defense Counsel submitted that though the complainant failed to prove that any legal notice was ever sent to the accused but even if the said fact be assumed for the sake of arguments, even then no offence u/s 138 of the NI Act was made out against the accused as the legal notice was not sent within the requisite period of fifteen days from the date of receipt of return memo from the bank, as requied by proviso (b) to Section 138 of the NI Act. It was, therefore, contended by Ld. Defense Counsel that the present complaint was not legally maintainable and the accused was entitled to acquittal. 19. The above contention may now be dealt. Proviso (b) to Section 138 of the CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 10 Negotiable Instruments Act , as it stood prior to the coming into effect of the Negotiable Instruments (Amendment and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2002, required sending of demand notice within a period of fifteen days from the date of receipt of intimation regarding the dishonour of cheque. The said period of 15 days had expired on 12.07.2002 in the present case. The legal notice was issued on 31.07.2002, i.e., after the period of 15 days was over. 20. In S.V. Muthye Vs State & Anr. 96 (2002) DLT 718 it was observed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court as follows: "8. Subsection (2) of Section 142 provides that a complaint for the offence under Section 138 has to be made within one month of the date on which cause of action arises under Clause (c) of the proviso to Section 138 . To be noted that aforementioned decisions pertain to condoning the delay in filing the complaint and not the delay in serving the demand notice under Clause (b) of said Section 138. Serving of notice within 15 days of the receipt of intimation regarding dishonour of cheque by the payee and failure to make payment within 15 days of receipt of notice issued under Clause (b) of Section 138 by the drawer are to precede the filing of complaint under Section 138 . In the matter of condoning delay in issuing demand notice beyond the statutory period of 15 days neither Section 473 Cr.P.C. or Section 5 of Limitation Act, 1963 would apply nor such a delay can be legally condoned." 21. The ratio of S.V. Muthye (supra) was also followed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Kailash Engineers Vs Auto Pins (I) Ltd. 2003 (67) DRJ 782. 22. It is clear from the above judgment that issuance of legal demand notice within CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand 11 15 days (as it stood at the relevant time) after the receipt of information of dishonour of cheque by the complainant is a sine qua non for filing a complaint u/s 138 NI Act and delay in issuing the said legal notice is not legally condonable. In view of the same, I hold that the present complaint case is not maintainable. 23. Ld. Counsel for the accused also argued that there was no liability of the accused in favour of the complainant on the date the chques in question were handed over to the complainant and that the same were given for the purpose of security. Ld. Counsel also argued that the complainant failed to prove the extent of liablity of the accused on the date of the cheques in question. However, as the accused is entitled to acquittal on the pure legal preposition of legal notice not being sent within the stipulated period of 15 days from the date of receipt of dishonour memo (as the law stood at the relevant time), I am refraining from giving a finding on the above further contentions. Order 24. In view of my finding on question (ii) above, accused Gopi Chand is acquitted of the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Announced in open Court on (JAGMOHAN SINGH) 25th April, 2013 (11 pages) M.M. (NI Act )-08/Dwarka, 25.04.2013 CC No. 734/12, DSCF vs Gopi Chand
